Quotes state the execution role holds every permission the function needs to access other AWS resources, every function must have one, resource-based policies grant other accounts and AWS services access, and when a service such as S3 calls the function Lambda considers only the resource-based policy.

How IAM works lists actions or operations, resources, principal, environment data (IP, user agent, SSL status, timestamp) and resource data, then says AWS gathers them into a request context which IAM evaluates to authorize the request.

Quotes state temporary credentials are short-term, not stored with the user but generated dynamically when requested, AWS no longer recognizes them or allows API access after expiry, and they cannot be reused.
